 Open Navigation Menu Menu Style 10 Photos of Harrison Ford, Hollywood Heartthrob, at Home
 Long before he made a name for himself as a blockbuster star, Harrison Ford was an enthusiastic working carpenter – see the actor with his handiwork in these 10 throwback images By Juliana Ukiomogbe November 8, 2026 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Whether he's best known for his role as Han Solo or as Indiana Jones, heartthrob Harrison Ford is certainly a Hollywood favourite , famous for conquering some of its biggest film franchises. But away from the set, Ford was busy quietly curating an enviable real estate collection. After leaving his native Chicago for Tinseltown, the actor acquired several standout abodes across California before eventually settling on a sprawling mountain ranch in Wyoming.
 Amid his rising global stardom, Ford made a conscious effort to protect his time at home. “The way it is now, I do one film a year usually,” he told the Los Angeles Times in 2000. “And it leaves me just enough time to be with my family and to pursue the other interests that I have.” About his family life, he added, “I want my kids to enjoy their privacy. There is no reason why they should be dragged into this fishbowl with me.” Below, we look back at 10 images of Ford enjoying life outside the Hollywood glare.
 Beyond the screen
 Ford doing some cleaning at home in 1981.
 Photo: Nancy Moran/Sygma via Getty Images Before breaking through as a Hollywood lead, Ford made his living as a self-taught carpenter. His first major break came after securing a minor role in George Lucas’s 1973 film American Graffiti , produced by Francis Ford Coppola. Soon after, Coppola hired him to install custom entrance joinery at his production offices. “He appealed to me,” Ford told Esquire in 2023. “I said I would do it but only at night, when no one was around, because I didn’t want to be that guy – I wanted them to think of me as an actor, which I was. I did the job.”
 The gig later unexpectedly opened the door for his role in Star Wars . “While I’m finishing up, first thing in the morning, in walked George Lucas and Richard Dreyfuss to begin the process of meeting people for Star Wars ,” Ford continued. “George had told our agents he wanted new faces, not the same people from American Graffiti. I was there with my tool belt on, sweeping up, said hello, chatted, and that was it. Later, I was asked by the producer to help them read lines with candidates for all the parts. Don’t know whether I read with people who were reading for Han Solo – can’t remember. I read with quite a few princesses. But there was no indication or forewarning that I might be considered for this part. It was just a favour. And then, of course, they offered me the part.”
 Benedict Canyon
 Ford poolside at his Benedict Canyon home.
 Photo: Nancy Moran/Sygma via Getty Images Captured at his Benedict Canyon home in 1981, Ford occupied a barn-style abode that was originally built in 1941 – the year before he was born. As Garry Jenkins noted in his 1996 biography Harrison Ford: Imperfect Hero , the actor wanted it to feel like his childhood home in the Chicago suburb of Park Ridge, Illinois. So he filled the space with Early American furniture, polished the wooden floors, and installed new doors. What he couldn’t find in furniture shops, he crafted himself. “Everything I built is still standing,” he told Parade in 2020. “The last time that I packed up my tools to go do a movie, I had no idea I wouldn’t unpack them again. And that was Star Wars .”
 A Hollywood leading man
 Ford reads in his home spa in this 1981 shot.
 Photo: Nancy Moran/Sygma via Getty Images By 1981, Ford was a bonafide movie star. He had just appeared in The Empire Strikes Back and was gearing up for the release of Raiders of the Lost Ark . In 2023, Ford reflected on his career as an actor. “I think it’s the place I feel most useful,” he told The Hollywood Reporter . “It’s what I know the most about. I lost my chops as a carpenter. I haven’t ever played fiddle. But I feel comfortable wrestling with how to make behaviour out of words on a page and tell a story, and I’m still excited about the prospect of telling a story. I think this is a service occupation – telling stories. We need it. Whether it’s drawing on caves or religious tenets, we love telling stories.”
 Mandeville Canyon
 Ford in 1984 in his Brentwood dwelling.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Ford was married to his second wife, the late screenwriter Melissa Mathison, from 1983 to 2004. The couple and their two children, Malcolm and Georgia, lived in Brentwood’s Mandeville Canyon neighbourhood. The actor is pictured at the home in this 1984 photo; he purchased the residence the year prior for $1 million. It was originally built in 1951 and designed by architect Gerard Colcord. Located a stone’s throw from the Getty Museum, the 7,164-square-foot home featured luxe amenities including two guesthouses, a library, and a wine cellar.
 DIY
 Ford is a self-taught carpenter.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Ford made several items of furniture for his Mandeville Canyon home, including tables and chairs. About his work, he once said , “Through carpentry, I fed my family and began to pick and choose from among the roles offered. I could afford to hold out until something better came along. But I never gave up my ambition to be an actor. I was frustrated but never felt defeated by my frustration.”
 A reluctant homemaker
 The actor doing some dishes at home in the ’80s.
 Photo: Nancy Moran/Sygma via Getty Images According to Jenkins’s biography, neither Ford nor Mathison were particularly skilled at homemaking. “We specialise in what we call ‘meals in minutes,’” he reportedly said. But once they started entertaining famous dinner guests, like director Ridley Scott, they made more of an effort to become excellent hosts. Ford would later star in Scott’s 1982 film Blade Runner .
 Years later, Ford reflected on his workaholic nature. “I can tell you this: If I’d been less successful, I’d probably be a better parent,” he told Esquire , later adding, “I accept my flaws and my failures – I don’t accept them, I own them. And certainly the more constant gardener is the better parent, and I’ve been out of town, up my own ass, for most of my life.”
 An A-list legacy property
 Ford made tables and chairs for his home when he was married to Mathison and living in Mandeville Canyon.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Ford lived in his Mandeville Canyon home for 29 years before he sold it to Kevin Reilly, former chief content officer of HBO Max, for $8.2 million in 2012 . Reilly owned the house for only four years before he handed the keys to Evan Spiegel, CEO of Snapchat, who bought it for $12 million in 2016. Spiegel and his wife, the model Miranda Kerr, whom he married the following year, lived at the estate for eight years before offloading it for $16 million .
 The Wyoming wilderness
 Ford on his home’s patio in the ’80s.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images In addition to owning a spot in California , Ford and Mathison lived in an 800-acre home in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. According to Harrison Ford: Imperfect Hero , he bought a home along the Snake River for nearly $1 million. “I think we all get something set in our heads early on,” he reportedly said. “And the first time I saw Jackson Hole, I said, ‘This is the place that’s been in my mind all the time.’” He particularly loved the nature, adding, “It was about water, streams, trees, animals, a grand expression of nature – the Tetons rising sharply from a flat, high mountain plateau.” Jenkins also reported that Ford was given the option to either buy the home and a few acres of land or the entire tract. He decided to buy all the land, and later said, “It had everything I wanted.”
 Away from the madness
 Ford at home in 1984, with a whimsical sculpture posed twirling overhead.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Ford, who is pictured here in 1984 at home in Southern California , felt that few other showbusiness fixtures were venturing to set up home bases outside Tinseltown. “I don’t think anybody was doing what I did; I don’t know anybody,” he told The Hollywood Reporter . “Once people are established to a certain degree, they don’t have to be at a roll call in Hollywood – which is a fictional place, anyway. This is Los Angeles. We call the movie business ‘Hollywood.’ But the movie business is everywhere now. It’s in Atlanta. It’s in New Orleans. People are building studios in Montana with a big investment. The question is: How do you want to spend your life? How much freedom do you have against how much freedom do you want? Do you care if you miss roles or not? Do you want to be there for everything? I lived in Los Angeles for a long time before I left. I wanted it for my kids.”
 Harrison Ford’s current LA home
 Ford in 1984.
 Photo: Paul Harris/Getty Images Ford married actor Calista Flockhart in 2010. The couple, who share a son, purchased a residence in Mandeville Canyon, the same area where the actor is pictured at home here in 1984, for $12.65 million shortly after tying the knot. The gated home sits on 13,767 square feet and features seven bedrooms , nine bathrooms, six fireplaces, a backyard cottage, a wood-panelled library, a game room, and a swimming pool. The couple still owns this property, and Ford continues to split his time between California and Wyoming.
